artifactType: independent implementation review of additive v4 source-frame cache hardening

reviewer.scope: source identity/cache correctness and reproducibility only

engineeringFindings.result: passes independent code review and executable tests
engineeringFindings.evidence: v4 validates the loaded source path/hash at binding, retains the bound document object, and checks page.parent/document identity before reading or writing the direct cache. Direct keys include source SHA, document identity, page ordinal, clip, target hash/dimensions, effective DPI candidates and store policy.
The test drives actual legacy v3 and v4 direct pixmap calls around a full-page image render: v3 misses after the render-order perturbation and v4 matches after store clearing before each pixmap.

engineeringFindings.result: passes independent code review and test coverage
engineeringFindings.evidence: The full-page identity includes verified source SHA, ordinal, renderer/version, DPI, RGB mode, measured dimensions, decoded RGB hash and MuPDF store policy; sidecar, payload, dimensions and full key are validated on cache hit.
The fresh v4 full report SHA is pinned; I independently compared all 3,396 row records, 3,399 owner-use records and status counts against the frozen v3 full report and found deep equality.

result.status: independently approved for the bounded cache/source-binding/render-order correction

scopeLimitations: V4 inherits v3 normalizedPageRect parsing. I independently counted 541 current rows whose only normalizedPageRect keys are x/y/w/h and verified the v4 output has zero direct/full-page recipes for those rows. They are unsupported-schema cases, not exhausted searches; v5 is authorized to add explicit support.
The 151 other unresolved rows have supported normalized schemas and were subjected to the recorded finite replay; they remain exact-pixel unresolved.
The reported 692 unresolved comprises both populations and should not be called uniformly exhausted.
Exact raster replay does not approve semantic source coverage, source interpretation, transcription, crop relevance/focus, citation grade, or the unavailable historical 726-member census.
